summary: The thesis remains defendable as methodological work, but readiness dropped from 7.1 to 6.6 because active chapter sources now contain explicit user-test TODO placeholders and the promised participant study is still not executed. The strongest defensible contribution is a multidimensional validation protocol for low-resource wake-word detection, demonstrated on Estonian Kuule Kratt.
top_strengths: Abstracts and discussion now align better around methodology, reproducible pipeline, and evidence discipline.
The three audit-ring story remains strong: leakage, positive-label/fraasi-terviklikkus, and checkpoint-FAPH shortcut failures each produce a concrete metric expansion.
User-test tooling/protocol state improved: recorder, validator, replay, summarizer, two-tier consent, and questionnaire docs exist.
LaTeX build is healthy: 86-page PDF, no undefined refs/citations found; remaining issues are mostly overfull boxes and text placeholders.
Discussion is honest about negative results and does not treat low FAPH as equivalent to usability.
top_risks: Active results chapter contains TODO placeholders for user-test results.
20-30 participant final user test is still promised but not run.
Contribution hierarchy remains split between model, FAPH methodology, ESP32/HA integration, and methodological validation protocol.
Methodology promises CIs for every metric, but several tables still report point estimates only.
Threshold/user-test freeze policy is still a candidate with blank final freeze fields.
